title: Uncovering Shortcut Amplification in Video RLVR through the Lens of Perceptual Uncertainty Collapse
abstract: arXiv:2610.37211v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as an effective post-training paradigm for enhancing the video reasoning capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). Despite its empirical effectiveness, we show that outcome-level optimization can introduce an undesirable shortcut amplification effect, whereby models increasingly favor text-prior answers even when they are not supported by the visual evidence. To characterize this behavior, we investigate the training dynamics of video RLVR through the lens of perceptual uncertainty, analyzing how predictive uncertainty evolves under video-conditioned and text-only contexts. Our analysis identifies a perceptual uncertainty collapse phenomenon, in which RL training continuously sharpens the model's answer distribution while the uncertainty reduction attributable to visual evidence progressively diminishes. translated_title: 通过感知不确定性坍缩的视角揭示视频RLVR中的捷径放大效应
translated_abstract: 基于可验证奖励的强化学习（RLVR）已成为增强大型多模态模型（LMMs）视频推理能力的一种有效后训练范式。尽管其在实践中表现出有效性，我们表明结果层面的优化会引入一种不良的捷径放大效应，即模型越来越倾向于依赖文本先验答案，即使这些答案缺乏视觉证据的支持。为了刻画这一行为，我们通过感知不确定性的视角研究视频RLVR的训练动态，分析预测不确定性在视频条件和纯文本条件下如何演变。我们的分析识别出一种感知不确定性坍缩现象：RL训练持续使模型的答案分布变得尖锐，而归因于视觉证据的不确定性降低却逐渐减弱。进一步的梯度方向分析揭示了这种自信……
tldr: 本文揭示了视频RLVR后训练中存在捷径放大效应——模型在结果优化过程中日益依赖文本先验而忽视视觉证据，并通过感知不确定性坍缩现象对这一退化行为进行了系统刻画。
en_tdlr: This paper uncovers a shortcut amplification effect in video RLVR, where outcome-level optimization drives models to increasingly favor text-prior answers over visual evidence, and characterizes this degradation through the lens of perceptual uncertainty collapse.
